$status: draft — frozen when Stage 0 screens are approved
$source: docs/design/study/fingerprint.html, section 02 The system (flow decisions 65 to 68); motion from docs/design/motion-spec.md (flow decision 73)

surface.use: Groups, cards, fields, the mini player

line.use: Hairlines between rows and around cards (decorative, no contrast minimum)

line-strong.use: Field and chip edges, the empty slots (non-text, 3:1)

fill.use: Every filled control: primary buttons, the active segment, the active tab tile, play discs, the swipe reveal

on-fill.use: Content on any fill, including success and error fills

success.use: Done, connected; only where the text says the same thing

warning.use: Not written down (the recovery code); only where the text says the same thing

error.use: Delete, failures; only where the text says the same thing

fill.use: The fill rule (flow decision 66): the fill is the text colour and content on it is the page colour. Ink with paper on it in light, paper with ink on it in dark, and in the Reader the palette's own text and page (reader fill and on-fill). Success and error fills follow it too: their content is on-fill. There is no brand fill, no tint and no gradient; the covers are the only colour in the app.

focus.use: A 2 px ring in the focus colour, 2 px outside the control, so it sits on the page and never on the fill (ink on ink would vanish). Inside the Reader use reader focus; inside the inverted toast the scheme flips, so focus is the toast's own content colour.

cover.module: The generator (sha256 of the normalised URL, the hash in the d tag, contract 4.3) lives in the cover module with its own palette tables and OKLCH maths. It is versioned as cover v1, never edited once frozen, and checked by golden fixtures in every platform's CI. These tokens hold only the chrome around covers.

edge.use: An inset 1 px hairline on every cover (ink at 9% in light, paper at 10% in dark) so dark grounds don't bleed into the page

grey.use: A save whose text couldn't be fetched keeps its shapes, drawn in these chrome greys at full strength in place of its four inks. They follow the theme; every other cover is identical in both themes.

ink.use: The one ink an article lends to lines and marks: its progress lines, link underlines, the toast countdown, Speed read's focus ticks, the word meter and the waiting dot (the focus letter itself sits on the highlight, flow decision 71). It is the first of its cover inks that clears 3:1 on the background under it, else its signal ink mixed towards the fallback in 10% steps, else the fallback (the text colour of that surface). Set per article by the cover module (lineInk), as --reader-ink in the Reader. 3:1 suits lines and large text only; small text stays the text colour.

highlight.use: The spoken-word highlight, also the wash under Speed read's focus letter (flow decision 71): the article's signal ink washed into the page, starting at 34% and stepping down until the text on it keeps 7:1. Set per article by the cover module (highlight), as --reader-highlight. The static reader highlights below are the same rule with the muted colour as the wash, used only before an article's own value is applied.

reader.use: The same float inside the Reader, built from the reading palette: a hairline ring of reader muted at 28% and a soft drop, so the Reader dock, the mini player and Archive float correctly on any palette whatever the app theme.

float.use: The one shadow: only for things that hover over content (the mini player, the Reader dock, Archive, the toast). In dark the drop is all but invisible and the 1 px hairline ring carries it. Everything in the flow is flat, separated by 1 px hairlines; cards and groups have a line edge and no shadow in both themes.

scrim.use: The dimmed screen behind a sheet (z 40 in the consistency spec), fading in and out on the enter and exit motion. It follows the app theme in the Reader too, since sheets keep the app's surface whatever the reading palette. Light is ink at 46%, the lowest whole-byte alpha at which a white sheet's top edge keeps 3:1 against anything behind it: 3.03 on a dimmed white card, 3.32 on dimmed paper, 3.52 on a dimmed Sepia page. Dark is black at 60%. No scrim can lift the #1A1A1C sheet more than 1.21:1 off a dark page, so in dark the edge is the float shadow's 1 px ring. Black takes the page below graphite, where a graphite scrim cannot (ring 1.79 and sheet 1.17 on the dimmed page, against 1.67 and 1.09 undimmed), and at 60% the text, covers and light reading pages behind stay bright enough for the ring to show on them too (1.75 on dimmed text, where the sheet's own step is 2.69). Mid greys such as muted dim to the ring's level, and there the sheet's step (1.73) carries the edge. Figures are measured in headless Chrome from the rendered pixels.

ui.stack: 'Archivo', Roboto, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

sizeUse.13: meta, chips, segments, tab labels, the speed pill; nothing smaller
sizeUse.20: empty-state and sheet headings, at normal width
sizeUse.28: screen titles (display) and the Reader's article title
sizeUse.32: big counts on You (decision 68), in the display face

display.stack: 'Archivo', 'Archivo Expanded', 'Roboto Flex', Roboto, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif
display.use: Archivo Expanded (width axis 125): screen titles 28/1.2 and the big counts. One family with a width axis gives two voices without a third font.

mono.stack: 'Martian Mono', 'Roboto Mono', ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace
mono.use: Player clocks only (2:00 / 5:52), so the digits never shuffle

night.hue: the cover's hue in whole degrees (palette.hue in the cover module): bytes 0 and 1 of the d-tag hash as a 16-bit number × 360 / 65536, rounded, so 0 to 360, where 360 draws as 0
night.gamut: chroma is reduced until the colour fits sRGB; hue and lightness are kept
night.use: Night paper is tinted with each article's hue at very low chroma, so each article reads on its own dark paper. The cover module sets --reader-bg, --reader-text and --reader-muted from this rule (and fill, on-fill, link and focus follow them); the static night values above are the same rule at zero chroma, used only until an article is in view.

reader.use: id is the Aa sheet's value and the data-reader attribute (light and dark follow the app theme until Sepia is chosen); label is the Aa sheet's copy, unchanged. Link text is the text colour; its underline is the article ink.

fonts.use: The HTML mockups and the website load the web fonts. The Android app and the extension bundle the font files (variable Archivo with its width axis, Literata with optical sizes, Martian Mono) and never fetch them.

radius.use: 4 covers in lists and article images. 8 chips, segments, the active tab tile, the speed pill and cover play buttons. 12 buttons, fields and icon buttons. 14 every card and group, players, the toast and Archive. 20 sheets, illustrations and the viewfinder. Pill only for genuinely round ends: play discs, switch tracks, progress lines and dots.

instant.use: Values the system changes, set in one frame with no transition: clocks, counts, 'N min left', You's big counts, restore's 'N of M', Speed read's words, the spoken-word highlight, live progress, search results per keystroke and the toolbar badge. Numbers are in tabular figures. Reanimated: assign sv.value directly. There is no CSS property, since there is no transition.

enter.use: Every arrival and anything settling: layers rising 24 px into the bottom stack (toast, mini, Reader tier), sheets from 100% with the scrim, pushed screens 24 px from the right, gaps opening, stack offsets changing, the player changing tier both ways, a line's jump (±15, a sentence swipe, a restore step), follow-scroll steps, a sheet's top edge after a height change, the Aa palette plates. Reduced motion keeps the duration and drops the travel. Reanimated: withTiming(v, { duration: 250, easing: Easing.bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) }).

exit.use: Every removal, as the exact reverse of its enter: toast, mini and Reader tier sinking 24 px, sheets and scrim, pops, full-screen modes closing, the held press layer lifting. Reduced motion keeps the duration and drops the travel. Reanimated: withTiming(v, { duration: 200, easing: Easing.bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1) }).

quick.use: Crossfades inside a screen, both legs starting together: state swaps, selection layers, notices' and errors' text, glyphs, labels, skeleton to text, photos, the bar title, tab content. With 6 px of travel inside a clipped box it is the roll (the speed pill, Default speed and wpm), in the direction of the change; taps under 100 ms apart swap without it, and reduced motion swaps at once. Reanimated: in withTiming(1, { duration: 150, easing: Easing.bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) }), out withTiming(0, { duration: 100, easing: Easing.bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1) }); for layout, FadeIn.duration(150).easing(...) and FadeOut.duration(100).easing(...) on the same curves; or Reanimated 4 CSS transitions on opacity.

reflow.use: Siblings closing a gap, reordering, controls making room for ✕, played as FLIP on translateY and never on height. Opening a gap is enter. Reduced motion closes the gap at once. Reanimated: LinearTransition.duration(200).easing(Easing.bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)) as itemLayoutAnimation, or a translateY FLIP.

press.use: Every tappable: a flat state layer on the control's shape, in at once when a finger lands (60 ms late inside scrolling lists, so a flick never lights the rows it passes) and out on quick out. Ink at 8% on paper and surfaces (the text colour, so paper in dark), the page colour at 12% on fills, the reading text at 8% on reader surfaces. No ripple and no scale; unchanged under reduced motion, since it is opacity. CSS: an :active layer. Reanimated: press in sv.value = 1, press out withTiming(0, { duration: 100, easing: Easing.bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1) }); unstable_pressDelay={60} on list rows, and no android_ripple.

mark.use: Earned marks only, from opacity 0 and scale 0.4 (the extension's markIn keyframes): the share sheet's check, the extension's corner mark, All read's check, restore done, delete step results, options Connected and Sent. It is a cover leaf's arrival, shorter. A mark that belongs to a save lands with its cover's last leaf, never later than 1 s after the drawing starts. Never on a later visit. Reduced motion: a 150 ms fade with no scale. Reanimated: withTiming(1, { duration: 200, easing: Easing.bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) }) driving scale 0.4 + 0.6 × p and opacity p.

release.use: The one spring, only when a finger lets go: a swipe flying off or returning, a dragged sheet closing or settling back, a predictive-back cancel, Speed read's word returning after a short drag. Critically damped (damping ratio 1.0) and clamped, so it never overshoots: 90% of the way by about 190 ms, within 1% by about 320 ms. It is seeded with the release velocity, and a finger can catch it mid-flight. Reanimated: withSpring(to, { mass: 1, stiffness: 439, damping: 42, velocity, overshootClamping: true }). duration and easing are the spring from rest as a CSS linear() curve, for the prototypes only. Reduced motion: the drag still follows the finger, a release that commits fades over 200 ms instead, and one that cancels is back at rest at once.

draw.use: Signature 1 (Drawn once) only: a new save's cover drawing itself, each shape scaling in from 30% about its own cell in hash order, once per save and never on scroll, a tab switch, a remount, Undo or a palette change. 34 ms is Shelf's one stagger; the Reader tier's three controls reuse it. The cover module (ShelfCover.motion.once, ShelfCover.css) holds the numbers the app reads. Reduced motion shows the cover already drawn. Reanimated: read ShelfCover.motion.once at runtime; leaf n: p = clamp((t − start − 34n) / 520, 0, 1), e = Easing.bezierFn(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)(p), scale 0.3 + 0.7e about the cell's centre, opacity e, with one frame clock for every drawing cover.

catchUp.use: Signature 2 (One line, carried) only. Catch-up: on a pop back to the list that opened the article, once the stored position has moved by 2% (threshold) or more, that row's line moves from where it stood when the article opened to where it stands now, starting 150 ms after the pop begins and done about 550 ms after the tap; Welcome's front card runs it with no delay from the front cover's last leaf. Finish: archiving from the Reader completes the row's line to full from 100 ms into the pop, then the row leaves by row out (fill 100–300 ms, row fades 300–400 ms, gap closes 400–600 ms). With the draw-in, the only motion longer than 300 ms. Reduced motion sets the line at once, and Finish becomes a 200 ms fade of the row with the gap closing at once. Reanimated: withDelay(150, withTiming(p, { duration: 400, easing: Easing.bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) })); Finish withDelay(100, withTiming(1, { duration: 200, easing: Easing.bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) })).

countdown.use: The 2 px countdown lines, linear over the whole timeout: phone toasts getRecommendedTimeoutMillis(5000), the share sheet getRecommendedTimeoutMillis(4000), the extension's toast and popup 8000 ms. The values here are the base timeouts; Android may lengthen the phone's for the person's accessibility timeout. A full-width fill translated left inside an overflow-hidden strip, never width or scaleX, held while touched, hovered or focused or under a sheet's scrim, then run on with the time left. Hidden while a screen reader is on, when nothing auto-dismisses. Unchanged under reduced motion, since it carries information. CSS: an animation on transform, linear, with animation-play-state for the hold. Reanimated: withTiming(-W, { duration: remaining, easing: Easing.linear }); cancelAnimation to hold, then run again with the time left.

ambient.use: Waiting only, shown after 150 ms of waiting (delay), so a quick answer never shows it. Breathe: waiting dots and squares, opacity 0.3 to 1 and back, the three dots 200 ms apart in phase. Pulse: skeleton lines and an arriving photo's placeholder, opacity 0.55 to 1 and back (the shimmer is retired). Sweep: the Saves sync line's 30% segment along its track on translateX. Scan: the viewfinder's scan line on translateY, alternating. Eq: the voice sample's three bars on scaleY from the bottom, never height. Scaffold: the first-run slot's cover drawing on a loop through ShelfCover.css's loop class and ShelfCover.motion.loop, the only loop a cover has. Reduced motion: loops rest at full opacity (the scaffold drawn and still, the equaliser's bars still), except the Saves sync line, whose whole track breathes in place, since it has no words beside it. CSS: the prototype's keyframes on transform and opacity only. Durations are CSS cycles: breathe, pulse and eq go there and back within one, so each Reanimated leg is half of it; scan alternates whole cycles; sweep runs one way and starts again. Reanimated: withRepeat(withTiming(...), -1, true) with Easing.bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1) for ease-in-out (reverse false for sweep); the scaffold from ShelfCover.motion.loop.

motion.use: The motion spec (docs/design/motion-spec.md, flow decision 73). Fade by default, and travel only to show where something went. Two curves: enter for anything arriving or settling, exit for anything leaving, and linear only for clocks. One spring, critically damped, only when a finger lets go (release). One stagger, the cover's 34 ms. Two signatures: a cover draws once when its save lands (draw), and each article's line is carried from surface to surface and catches up with the reading just done (catchUp). Only transform and opacity animate; colour changes are stacked layers crossfading. Nothing waits for motion, and any input retargets it. Reduced motion keeps every meaning and drops the travel; in the app, read the setting at launch and on change, branch explicitly, and pass ReduceMotion.Never to the fallback fades.

icons.use: Lucide at 1.75 to sit with Archivo's finer stems. Icons are text or muted, never coloured; the active tab sits in an inverted tile (radius control). The custom icons are decision 62's skip ±15 pair and Shelf's own speed-read icon. The pair's 15 is drawn at 1.3125, three quarters of the stroke (docs/design/icons/app/README.md), so a platform that overrides the stroke sets the numerals to 0.75 of it.

changelog: 0.1.0 (2026-09-27): Soft pills, Terracotta accent, Lucide icons chosen by Richard. Added on-accent (a tenth colour) because text on an accent fill must be white in light mode and near-black in dark mode, where white on #CA8469 fails contrast (2.8:1). Contrast checked: accent on surface 4.9:1 light, 6.1:1 dark; muted on background 6.7:1 light, 6.6:1 dark. Accent text on accent-soft is 4.3:1 in light mode, below AA for small text, so soft chips use the text colour for labels and the accent only for icons.
0.1.1 (2026-09-27): dark muted raised from #94979C (6.2:1 on surface) to #B4B7BD (9.0:1). Richard found the old grey hard to read on dark cards at 13 px despite passing AA.

0.1.2 (2026-09-27): reader palette added (light, sepia, dark) because the Aa sheet offers Sepia and the nine app colours have no sepia. Reader dark text is #E4E4E6 rather than #F7F7F7 to soften glare over long reading. Contrast: sepia text 11:1, sepia muted 5.3:1. Reader links: Terracotta on light (4.6:1), brand-700 #944526 on sepia (5.8:1, since #B5542E is only 4.25:1 there), #CA8469 on dark.

0.1.3 (2026-09-27): reader highlight per theme (light #EDD5CA after a first try at #F3E4DE was too faint to follow) (the spoken word while listening); accent-soft was too close to the sepia background to see. radius.sheet 24 for bottom sheets and the floating player: at 10 a sheet reads as a card, not a surface sliding up.

0.1.4 (2026-09-27), from the prototype review: reader.palette.*.accent so reader surfaces (speed-read focus letter, progress lines, player strip) never inherit the app accent, which fell to 2.6:1 on Sepia with the phone in dark mode. shadow.float per theme for floating elements (extension toast, Archive button, illustrations), because appending to shadow.card breaks when it is none in dark mode. radius.image 8 for thumbnails and article images, and gap.card 10 for the space between cards as signed off in the UI brief. on-accent also colours glyphs on success and error fills, keeping them at 9.5:1 and 6.9:1 in dark mode.

0.1.5 (2026-09-27), from Richard: content on Terracotta is white everywhere (flow decision 61). Added fill.accent and fill.on. In dark mode the active segment and the swipe reveal were #CA8469 with near-black content; they now use fill.accent (#B5542E) with white. The Reader player and Speed read play buttons had been recoloured to the reader text colour (black in the light and sepia palettes) by a rule meant for their plain controls. on-accent now colours only content on success and error fills.

0.2.0 (2026-10-04), Fingerprint (flow decisions 65 to 68), taken from the system section of docs/design/study/fingerprint.html. Terracotta is retired: the brand ramp, the gradient, accent, accent-soft, on-accent, fill.accent, fill.on and shadow.card are gone from the live tokens (the frozen tokens-softpills.css keeps them for the Soft pills copies). The chrome is ink, paper, two greys and hairlines. The fill is the text colour and content on it is the page colour in both themes and every reading palette, which replaces decision 61's white-on-Terracotta rule and also covers success and error fills (on-fill replaces on-accent there). New colour roles: fill, on-fill, focus (the text colour), line-strong (field and chip edges) and warning (the recovery code's Not written down). Cards are flat with a line edge in both themes; one float shadow remains, carried by a 1 px hairline ring in dark, with a Reader variant built from the reading palette. Reading palettes are paper, sepia and night, still labelled Light, Sepia and Dark on the Aa sheet and keyed light, sepia and dark in data-reader. Night is tinted per article from the cover's hue (OKLCH page L 0.215 C 0.022, text 0.905/0.012, muted 0.745/0.022); the static night values are that rule at zero chroma. reader.accent becomes reader.ink, the fallback for the ink each article lends its progress line, link underline and Speed read focus letter; the cover module sets it and the spoken-word highlight per article. Added reader fill, on-fill and focus so the Reader never borrows the chrome's fill from the other theme. Type: Archivo for UI, Archivo at width 125 for display, Literata 18/1.6 with optical sizes for reading (Aa sheet 15 to 24), Martian Mono 13 for player clocks only; 32 is for decision 68's big counts. Radii: image 4 (was 8), control 8 (new), button 12 (new), container 14 (was 10), sheet 20 (was 24), pill kept for round ends only. Icons are Lucide at 1.75. Motion enter and exit move here unchanged from the consistency spec, plus the cover drawing (520 ms per shape, 34 ms apart). The app icon (decision 67) needs no token; the word meter and stamps (decision 68) use existing roles. Contrast, WCAG 2.x, measured from these hex values. Light, on paper / on surface: text 15.97 / 17.89, muted 6.07 / 6.81, success 4.70 / 5.26, warning 6.13 / 6.86, error 5.87 / 6.57; on-fill on fill 15.97, on success 4.70, on error 5.87; focus 15.97 / 17.89 and line-strong 3.08 / 3.45 (non-text, 3:1 needed); line 1.22 (decorative). Dark, on graphite / on surface: text 15.96 / 14.70, muted 7.66 / 7.06, success 8.92 / 8.21, warning 9.06 / 8.34, error 8.30 / 7.64; on-fill on fill 15.96, on success 8.92, on error 8.30; focus 15.96 / 14.70 and line-strong 4.39 / 4.05 (non-text); line 1.39 (decorative). Inverted toast, light page (ink toast, dark roles inside): title 15.97, muted 7.26, success 8.45, error 7.86. Dark page (paper toast, light roles inside): title 15.96, muted 5.76, error 5.56, success 4.45, the one pair under 4.5:1 (raised to 4.51 in 0.2.1). Reading, page / text on the static highlight: Paper text 15.72, muted 6.20, on-fill on fill 15.72, highlight 9.53; Sepia text 10.78, muted 5.44, on-fill 10.78, highlight 7.09; Night at zero chroma text 13.19, muted 7.75, on-fill 13.19, highlight 7.19. Per article, over the board's 8 sample hashes and 10,000 random ones: tinted Night text 13.11 to 13.30 and muted 7.64 to 7.82; text on the spoken-word highlight at least 10.37 on Paper, 7.30 on Sepia and 7.00 on Night; article ink at least 3.00 on paper, surface, Paper, Sepia and the dark-page toast, 4.89 on graphite, 4.51 on the dark surface, 4.64 on the light-page toast and 4.57 on Night.

0.2.1 (2026-10-04), fixes after the Fingerprint re-skin. Light success #1E7B4B becomes #1E7A4A so it clears 4.5:1 everywhere it sits: 4.51 on the paper toast of a dark page (was 4.45), 4.76 on paper (was 4.70), 5.33 on surface (was 5.26), and on-fill on a success fill 4.76 (was 4.70). Success can be text on the toast like any other role, so 0.2.0's tick-disc-only rule is dropped. Added scrim, the dimmed screen behind sheets, one value per theme: ink at 46% (#17171A76) in light and black at 60% (#00000099) in dark, chosen for the sheet's edge as the scrim entry explains (3.03:1 at worst in light; in dark the float shadow's ring, 1.79 on the dimmed page and 1.75 on dimmed text). It replaces the mockups' mixes (text at 40% in light, background at 72% in dark) and Soft pills' #0C0E1266. Text fixes: reader.night.hue is the hue rounded to whole degrees (palette.hue, 0 to 360), as the board and the cover module use it; icons.customDigitStroke is 1.3125, three quarters of the 1.75 stroke as the redrawn icons have it (it said 1.5, the stroke-2 value); article.ink no longer colours Speed read's focus letter, which sits on the spoken-word highlight in the reading text colour (flow decision 71), and its list of lines and marks now matches the consistency spec.

0.2.2 (2026-10-04), the motion spec, signed off as flow decision 73 (docs/design/motion-spec.md, its Tokens section). The motion group, which held enter, exit and the cover draw-in, gains the spec's other tokens. instant: no transition, for values the system changes. quick: in 150 ms on the enter curve and out 100 ms on the exit curve, for crossfades, and the roll with 6 px of travel. reflow: 200 ms on the enter curve, played as FLIP. press: a flat state layer, in at once (60 ms late in scrolling lists) and out on quick out; ink at 8% on paper and surfaces, the page colour at 12% on fills, the reading text at 8% on reader surfaces. mark: 200 ms on the enter curve from scale 0.4, for earned marks. release: the one spring, for a finger letting go (mass 1, stiffness 439, damping 42, clamped, seeded with the release velocity), with a 320 ms linear() curve standing in for it in the prototypes. catchUp: 400 ms on the enter curve after 150 ms, for a change of 2% or more, with Finish at 200 ms after 100 ms. countdown: linear on transform, 5000 ms on phone toasts, 4000 ms on the share sheet and 8000 ms in the extension. ambient: the waiting loops, shown after 150 ms: breathe 1200 ms, pulse 1400 ms, sweep 1200 ms, scan 1800 ms alternating, eq 1000 ms, and the first-run scaffold from the cover module's loop. Every token's use now gives its Reanimated call and its reduced-motion behaviour, enter, exit and draw included, and their values are unchanged. New CSS custom properties: --motion-quick-in, --motion-quick-out, --motion-reflow, --motion-mark and --motion-catchup as the spec names them, and, named after their tokens where the spec gives a value without a property, --motion-catchup-delay, --motion-catchup-finish, --motion-catchup-finish-delay, --motion-press-delay, --motion-press-layer, --motion-press-layer-fill, --motion-press-layer-reader, --motion-release, --motion-countdown-toast, --motion-countdown-share, --motion-countdown-extension, --motion-ambient-delay, --motion-ambient-breathe, --motion-ambient-breathe-phase, --motion-ambient-pulse, --motion-ambient-sweep, --motion-ambient-scan and --motion-ambient-eq. instant has no property, and the scaffold keeps ShelfCover.css's loop class. The TypeScript module for Reanimated that the spec's Before build asks for is not generated yet.
